sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Carrollton
sections.html:
Three options exist in Carrollton: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash buyer. Choosing cash trades some price for speed and no repair work. Choosing a listing trades time for the chance at a higher figure. Weigh your repair list, any liens and your moving date, then decide.

The city lies in parts of Dallas, Denton and Collin counties, and that affects everything that follows. Your appraisal district, tax bill and recording office all depend on which county your lot is in. Check the tax statement before you start.

Carrollton sits in the middle of the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. It has three DART light rail stations, including Downtown Carrollton Station on the Silver Line, and IH-35E, SH 121 and the President George Bush Turnpike run through or beside it. Houses near stations tend to appeal to commuters.

The city incorporated on June 14, 1913, and the older core holds houses from several eras. A house near the Elm Fork or an old creek bed may carry flood history, and a nearby house on Belt Line Road is recorded as flooding in 1908, the 1920s and the 1940s. If your lot sits low, a buyer may ask for flood insurance quotes, so pull together any claims history. Be ready for questions about commute time and school zoning, too.

Buyers also respond to what is close by. Downtown Carrollton centers on the Town Square, and the city lists sports complexes, hike and bike trails and a nature preserve among its amenities. Name the nearest one in your listing or when you talk with a buyer, since it is often what a family asks about first.

sections.h2: New short-term rentals are off the table
sections.html:
Carrollton passed Zoning Ordinance 4297 and Code Ordinance 4291 on December 2, 2025. No new short-term rental or bed and breakfast will be allowed, and only certain existing properties can qualify for a lodging license under Chapter 97 of the city code.

Carrollton rules for existing short-term rental operators
RequirementRule
Lodging licenseNeeded every year for each location
Ownership changeA new license and hotel occupancy tax number must be sought
Hotel occupancy taxRequired of all short-term rentals
Other rulesChapter 97, the zoning ordinance and other city codes apply

A license belongs to a specific owner and location, so a house that runs as a rental today may not be able to keep that use for a buyer. Say so early. Call Environmental Services at (972) 466-3060 for the status of your address.

With a city split across Dallas, Denton and Collin, the appraisal district and tax assessor change from parcel to parcel. The state rules are the same everywhere: January 1 sets value and the lien, and bills are due by January 31.

  • School districts give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A senior or disabled owner's school tax can be frozen.
  • Homestead appraisals are limited to a 10 percent annual increase, with exceptions for new additions.
  • Protests are due by the May deadline printed on your notice.

Ask the county that bills your parcel for a payoff figure, and whether an installment plan exists on any delinquent balance. Cities and counties may add local exemptions, so ask your county for the current list.

sections.h2: If property tax goes unpaid before a sale
sections.html:
An unpaid bill gets worse each month. Penalty and interest start after January 31, interest has no ceiling, and a lawyer retained by the taxing unit can add up to 20 percent.

  • Collectors may offer installment plans on delinquent tax, up to 36 months in some cases, and a plan is required for a residence homestead.
  • A tax lien lets the unit sue to foreclose even after the owner changes, so unpaid tax must be paid at or before closing.
  • Homestead land sold at a tax sale carries a two-year redemption right with a premium, so ask a lawyer what applies.
  • A former owner has two years to claim surplus from a tax sale.

Before you accept any offer, request a payoff from the tax office that bills your lot.

sections.h2: How a Carrollton deed is recorded
sections.html:
The county clerk where your lot sits takes the deed, which could be Dallas, Denton or Collin. Confirm the county before you send anything. A deed mailed to the wrong office costs you days at the end of a sale. Warranty, special warranty and quitclaim deeds all need a signature and acknowledgment, usually before a notary.

Recording fees add up by page, so let the title company quote the exact total. It usually pays them at closing and files for you. An old tax lien or a mechanic's lien that turns up must be cleared before a buyer can get clear title.

sections.h2: Inherited house or loan in default
sections.html:
For an inherited house, find out whether the estate used a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or an administration, since each leaves different paperwork for the county clerk. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement that no court checks, and buyers can refuse it.

With a loan in default, you have 20 days to reinstate. A notice of sale then goes out 21 or more days before a first Tuesday auction. Lenders have two years after the sale to sue for a deficiency. Selling before the auction date can keep equity that costs would otherwise eat.

Once you and a buyer agree, the title company opens the file. It confirms which county holds your parcel, requests payoffs from the tax office and any lender, and searches for liens. If a rental license or flood question exists, it goes into the disclosures now, not at the table. The deed is then drawn up, signed and acknowledged, and recorded with the right county clerk. If heirs are selling, the probate or affidavit paperwork is reviewed before any of that begins, because a title company will not close without proof of who may sign.

Collect the latest tax bill, any payoff letter, lease copies, and notes on flood history or rental licensing. A buyer can't see a house's past from the street, so a short written summary of repairs, claims and city licenses helps. Call City Hall at 972-466-3000 if you can't tell which office handles a permit or license question, and ask the clerk of your county how it wants a deed presented. A cash buyer who sees those documents on day one can make a firm offer and let the title company search the right county's records.

faqs.q: Which county is my Carrollton house in?
faqs.a: It could be Dallas, Denton or Collin, since the city lies in parts of all three. Your tax bill or the county appraisal district map shows which, and that decides where taxes are paid and the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I start a new short-term rental in Carrollton?
faqs.a: No. Ordinances passed December 2, 2025 allow no new short-term rental or bed and breakfast. Only certain existing properties can qualify for a lodging license, so call the city before assuming a rental use can continue.

faqs.q: Does a Carrollton lodging license pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. Licenses belong to a specific owner and location, and a change in ownership means a new license and hotel occupancy tax number must be sought.

faqs.q: How much homestead exemption do Carrollton schools give?
faqs.a: The school exemption is $140,000, and seniors or disabled owners get $60,000 more. Ask your county about local exemptions that may add to it.

faqs.q: Can Carrollton heirs sell without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A small estate affidavit works for qualifying estates, and a muniment of title can follow a court order. Without one of those routes, title may be hard to clear, so speak with the county clerk or a probate attorney.
